stem: Who was the founder of the Indian Association?
expl: On 26 July, 1876, Surendranath Banerjee, with the help of Anand Mohan Bose, founded the Indian Association in Calcutta. It was the most important among the contemporary organizations and, before the Congress, it was regarded as an all-India organization. This organization demanded reforms in the Civil Service examination system and launched movements on issues such as controversies like the Ilbert Bill. In the Indian Association (Bharat Sabha), the middle class was given priority over the zamindars.

stem: How many representatives took part in the first Session of the Indian National Congress?
expl: The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885 by A.O. Hume, a retired British officer. Its first session was held on 28–30 December, 1885 at the Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College in Bombay. A total of 72 delegates participated: 38 from the Bombay Province, 21 from Madras, 3 from Bengal, 7 from the North-Western Provinces and Awadh (present-day Uttar Pradesh), and 3 from Punjab. The first session of the Indian National Congress was presided over by Womesh Chandra Banerjee (W.C. Banerjee), and its first General Secretary was A.O. Hume himself.

stem: “The Indian National Congress was founded on the basis of Safety Valve Theory, to protect the British Government from threats.” Which leader said that?

stem: “In my belief, Congress is too tottering to its fall and one of my great ambitions while in India is to assist it to a peaceful demise.” Who wrote it?

options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The British rulers believed that the Congress, under the leadership of the moderates, was quite weak and had no deep roots among the masses; therefore, it could be finished. In a letter written by Curzon to the Secretary of State for India on 18 November 1900, he said: “In my belief, congress... peaceful demise.” In 1903, he wrote to the Governor of Madras: “Ever since I came to India, my policy has been to make the Congress impotent by every means.” In 1904, Curzon refused to meet a deputation led by the Congress President.

stem: The process of a split in the Congress in the early years of the twentieth century began over –

options.label: c
options.text: Participation of the people in the Congress Movement

expl: One major reason for the Congress split in the early years of the twentieth century was that the Moderates failed in their strategies and objectives, and they could not keep the common people with them. The Moderates did not work among the masses. They could not adjust their strategy according to political developments. They could not realise that their very achievements had made their politics impractical. The outlook and assessment of both the Moderates and the Extremists were also wrong—both in terms of their mutual differences and from a nationalist perspective. The Moderates could not understand that the government was negotiating with them mainly due to fear of the Extremists, and the Extremists could not understand that the Moderates could act as a protective shield in their struggle. As a result, the Congress split at the Surat session in 1907.

stem: The Congress took a critical stand over the Montford Reforms in 1918, which led to break up with the old moderate remnants (Sapru, Jayakar and Chintamani) who formed the

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: In August 1917, the Secretary of State for India, Edwin Montagu, made a historic statement in the British Parliament, known as the Montagu Declaration (August Declaration). In this declaration, it was proposed to increase the participation of Indians in administration and in the development of self-governing institutions in India. To work out these reforms, Montagu, along with the then Viceroy Lord Chelmsford, brought out a detailed report titled “Constitutional Reforms in India”, which is called the Montford Report or the Montagu–Chelmsford Report. This report was published in 1918. Regarding this report, differences between the liberal and extremist groups within the Congress became clearly visible. As a result, the liberals who supported the Montford Report separated from the Congress in 1918 and, under the leadership of Surendranath Banerjee, founded a new party in 1919 named the “Indian National Liberal Federation”.

stem: In which working Committee did the Congress adopt the policy of abolishing land ownership?
expl: The Executive Committee of the Indian National Congress adopted the policy of abolishing landlordism in 1937. Tenancy bills were passed in the United Provinces and Bihar. In all Congress-ruled provinces, efforts were made to protect cultivators from the clutches of moneylenders and to improve irrigation facilities.

stem: Who was the Congress President who held talks with both the Cripps Mission and Lord Wavell?
expl: Abul Kalam Azad remained the President of the Congress from 1940 to 1946. He held talks with both the Cripps Mission (in 1942) and Lord Wavell (in 1945).

stem: Who was the President of the Indian National Congress at the time of the partition of India?
expl: When India became independent, J.B. Kripalani was the President of the Congress. He was elected President at the Meerut Session of the Congress (November 1946), and he remained President at the time of Independence as well. The Jaipur Session of the Congress (December 1948) was presided over by Dr. Pattabhi Sitaramayya. Mahatma Gandhi presided over the Belgaum Session (1924); Jawaharlal Nehru presided over the Lahore, Lucknow and Faizpur Sessions (respectively: December 1929, April 1936 and December 1936); and Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel presided over the Karachi Session (March 1931).

stem: Who presided over the Delhi Session the of Indian National Congress in 1947?
expl: A special session of the Indian National Congress was held in Delhi on 14–15 June 1947. Although Acharya J.B. Kripalani was the President of the Congress then, this historic meeting was presided over by Dr. Rajendra Prasad. The main purpose of this meeting was to deliberate on the Mountbatten Plan.

stem: At the Congress Working Committee meeting at Allahabad (April-May 1947), who of the following members was able to secure a majority for his plan of a guerrilla War against the Japanese due to India’s unequivocal stand against Nazism, Fascism and imperialism?
expl: Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru, because of India’s firm anti-Nazism, anti-Fascism and anti-imperialist stand, secured a majority in support of his plan for guerrilla war against Japan in the Congress Working Committee meeting held at Allahabad (13 May 1942).

stem: In which of the following Indian National Congress Sessions, the resolutions related to the Fundamental Rights were passed for the first time?
expl: To approve the Gandhi–Irwin Pact (Delhi Pact), the Karachi Session of the Congress was held on 29–31 March 1931 under the presidentship of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. In this session, for the first time, the Congress passed resolutions related to Fundamental Rights and the National Economic Programme. In the same session, when some people opposed it, Gandhiji said, “Gandhi may die, but Gandhism will not.”
